description:
FOUND s494 (Fable, 2026-09-21) by the ENDURANCE battery (questions-worth-asking Q4; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/q4/cases/e04b-streval-dist.pl, run1.meta, run1a.log).  main 863d3e20, the user-facing `pcl`.
MEASURED: `for my $i (1 .. 3000) { $s += eval "$i + 1" }` -- perl 0.11 s; pcl 13.0 s (4.3 ms per DISTINCT string = the transpile-server round trip + the two file writes); ~/.pcl-cache/evals before 17,758 files / 72,348 KB, after 23,760 / 96,888 KB.  (The 17,758 that were already there come from the test runners -- the same growth, slower.)  RSS stays flat (90 -> 94 MB): the in-memory table grows by the text only.
WHY IT MATTERS: generated eval strings are a real idiom (accessor generators repeat -- those are what #1200's cache is FOR -- but templating engines, `eval "sub { $code }"` compilers, Safe-like evaluators and test generators do not repeat).  The 30-day prune (docs/caching.md: miss-only, once a day) bounds the directory across DAYS, not within a run; an inode-exhausted or quota-full home directory is a failure a user cannot connect to "I ran a script".
FIX SHAPE (policy, no new mechanism; docs/caching.md is the contract to update):
 1. A PER-PROCESS WRITE BUDGET with a hit test: the cache earns its keep only when strings repeat ACROSS runs.  After K disk-cache WRITES in one process (K ~ 64-256; measure on the Moo / JSON::PP loads, which are the cache's customers: how many distinct evals does `use Moo` + 20 `has` perform?) stop WRITING for the rest of the process; reads continue.  A module load stays fully cached; a generator loop stops littering.
 2. OR a size/cost floor: do not write an entry whose transpile was cheaper than the two file writes -- `1 + 1` costs more to cache than to redo.  Measure the distribution of eval TEXT length over the populations first (the sweep + the board: one histogram).
 3. `pcl --cache-info` should print the evals/ FILE COUNT beside its size (#1335 added the directory; a count is what reveals this).
WHAT COULD BREAK: #1200's win (`use JSON::PP; print 1` 1.13 -> 0.41 s) -- the bar is that this row does not move; the eval cache KEY discipline (s387: capture names + features + package) is untouched by a write policy.
BAR: e04b before -> after (files written <= the budget); the #1200 bench row unchanged; docs/caching.md updated; a tools/t or Pl/t row that runs K+10 distinct evals against a temp PCL_CACHE_DIR and counts files.
SIZE: filler, 1-2 h including the measurement.  Owner of the policy choice: Fable reviews the histogram.
subject: ENDURANCE / DISK: the string-eval DISK cache writes TWO files for EVERY distinct eval string, with no bound inside a run -- 3,000 distinct `eval "$i + 1"` strings added 6,002 files / 24.5 MB to ~/.pcl-cache/evals (17,758 -> 23,760 files); a program that evals a million generated strings writes 2M files / ~8 GB into the user's home directory, and gains nothing (no string ever repeats)
